notes: v1.14.573 — THE BUTTON OPENS WHAT THE HEADLINE PROMISES. Owner device FAIL on .572, fixed. ⛔ THE DEFECT: .572 computed the hero headline from masterLoaded/live and the CTA from cmd_nba() INDEPENDENTLY, so they could disagree — and on device they did: "98 racks on US-SPK03. Tap one." sat above a button reading GO TO HANDOFF. The headline promised the picker; the button opened the handoff. Names-say-what-the-door-opens, broken inside one card. ⚠ .572 own comment PREDICTED this risk and did not prevent it — predicting a hazard is not mitigating it. ⭐ THE RULE NOW: where the headline promises a SPECIFIC surface the CTA IS that surface and the NBA gets no vote (no Master → LOAD MASTER; active deployment → PICK A RACK → cmd_openPicker); where the headline promises nothing specific, the NBA supplies the door, which is what it is for. ⛔ AND THE NBA DOES NOT SILENTLY VANISH — THAT WOULD BE A REGRESSION, NOT A FIX: the .571 DOM census proved .nba paints NOTHING on the phone, so the hero CTA was its ONLY face, and taking the primary button from it would drop an open handoff draft or a blocker off the first screen entirely. Per the owner ruling it moves to a SECONDARY line (#cs-hero-sub), shown ONLY when the NBA points somewhere the primary button does not, so the card never states one destination twice, and hidden with no text and no handler when there is nothing to say (Contract B14). ⚠ Cold Aisle floor met via min-height var(--tap-s); the JS sets display:flex rather than clearing it, because a cleared inline display falls back to a div block default and the align-items would never apply. ⛔ NOT IN THIS SHIP: the below-the-fold Deck cards the owner saw are rows 2-9 of the confirmed table and are slices A-2/A-3/A-4.
